---

sddviz reads every entry's derived status from one view call, over the layout
`source(graph):as-list`, and matches the lines to entries by identifier.

sdd computes status from the whole graph and stores it nowhere. No embedding reaches that
computation: a snapshot reports its project, its revision and its health, and nothing further.
`source(graph)` is the unfiltered population, so closed and superseded entries arrive beside live
ones, and a line names the live entry that replaced a retired one.

Computing status inside sddviz loses. It needs no call and answers at once. Against that, it would
have to reproduce rules that are far from obvious. Supersession outranks closure. The reported closer
resolves forward to the live head of its chain. A closer that is itself superseded drops out. A
directive turns terminal through its own intent. Signals read open where decisions read active. Done
signals carry no status. Roles derive through a cascade over actor chains. Each rule is a way to show
a retired decision as live.

The line the status arrives on carries its own risk, and it is the smallest available. sdd documents
its shape and its own unit tests hold it, which makes it the firmest surface the tool offers a reader
outside it. The module reading it names the sdd version it targets.

Nothing follows from this on its own. It constrains work other entries commission.
